subject: [hw] V41 -> D01: encoder IPI/message facts, venc_vsi = 2016 bytes, header-mode and ENCODE_DONE gaps
body:
From V41 (MESSAGE_FLOW.md has the full annotated sequence). Facts for FACTS.md, all host-verified from the kernel tree; nothing here was run on the phone. Short path K = nord2-current-kernel/drivers/media/platform/mtk-vcodec.

[V] 1. The encoder IPI message ids are AP_IPIMSG_ENC_INIT 0xC000, SET_PARAM 0xC001, ENCODE 0xC002, DEINIT 0xC003, QUERY_CAP 0xC004; the VCU answers INIT_DONE 0xD000, SET_PARAM_DONE 0xD001, ENCODE_DONE 0xD002, DEINIT_DONE 0xD003, QUERY_CAP_ACK 0xD004, ENCODE_ACK 0xD005; the daemon's own requests are POWER_ON 0xE000, POWER_OFF 0xE001, WAIT_ISR 0xE002, PUT_BUFFER 0xE003. Evidence: K/venc_ipi_msg.h:13-15, :27-50.

[V] 2. Message sizes (32-bit daemon and 64-bit AP are identical, verified by compiling the kernel's venc_ipi_msg.h twice and diffing all sizeof/offsetof): ap_ipi_msg_init 16, ap_ipi_query_cap 24, vcu_query_cap_ack 40, ap_ipi_msg_set_param 48, ap_ipi_msg_enc 76, ap_ipi_msg_deinit 8, vcu_ipi_msg_common 16, vcu_ipi_msg_init 24, vcu_ipi_msg_set_param 48, vcu_ipi_msg_enc 32, vcu_ipi_msg_deinit 16, vcu_ipi_msg_waitisr 24. Evidence: ap/test_v41/probe_kernel.c vs probe_mine.c, 63 lines equal; armv7 AAPCS compile of ap/mtk_venc_ipi.h.

[V] 3. struct venc_vsi is 2016 bytes in this tree, not 1248: VIDEO_MAX_FRAME is 64 (uapi/linux/videodev2.h:73), so VENC_MAX_FB_NUM=64 (venc_ipi_msg.h:17) and struct ring_input_list is 1552; venc_vcu_config 220 (color_desc at 76), venc_info 184, sizeimage at 220, list_free at 256, venc at 1808, sync_mode 1992, meta_addr 2000, meta_fd 2008. Evidence: same oracle; struct definitions venc_ipi_msg.h:382-550.

[V] 4. The capability query is sent on IPI_VENC_COMMON (14), not on the session's codec id: vcu_enc_query_cap() maps a temporary instance id 0 to IPI_VENC_COMMON (K/venc_vcu_if.c:347), and the handler copies sizeof(element)*64 bytes from the VCU DMEM address it got (venc_vcu_if.c:27-56, elements 12 and 36 bytes). The ack carries ap_inst_addr and vcu_data_addr (venc_ipi_msg.h:165-190).

[V] 5. V4L2_CID_MPEG_VIDEO_HEADER_MODE is registered with max JOINED_WITH_1ST_FRAME and default SEPARATE (K/mtk_vcodec_enc.c:2753-2755). Consequently a stock stream start sends ONLY VENC_SET_PARAM_ENC; with SEPARATE the first encode job sends a sequence-header encode (VENC_BS_MODE_SEQ_HDR, no frame) and then the frame (m2mops_venc_device_run, mtk_vcodec_enc.c:2598-2615). PREPEND_HEADER is sent at stream start only in JOINED mode (mtk_vcodec_enc.c:1874-1892). Values for a stock 1080p30 H.264 session: input_yuv_fmt 6 (NV12), 1920x1080 visible / 1920x1088 coded, 30 fps, bitrate 20000000 (control default :2730), profile 0 BASELINE (:2757-2759), level 0 (:2761), GOP and intra period 0, VBR.

[V] 6. The kernel's vcu_enc_ipi_handler() has no case for VCU_IPIMSG_ENC_ENCODE_DONE (K/venc_vcu_if.c:123-179): state/is_key_frm/bs_size of that message are ignored, only signaled/failure are set. The normal result path is the free-buffer ring venc_vsi.list_free + VCU_IPIMSG_ENC_PUT_BUFFER (venc_get_free_buffers, venc_common_if.c:354-391; mtk_enc_put_buf, mtk_vcodec_enc.c:113-178). FRAME_FINAL reads vcu->bs_size (venc_common_if.c:213), which nothing in this tree ever writes - a second gap.

[V] 7. IPI queues are per instance slot, handlers per id: ipi_id_to_inst_id() puts every VENC id (>= IPI_VENC_COMMON) in slot VCU_VENC=1 and every VDEC id in slot 0 (K/mtk_vcu.c:118-125); user_obj[VCU_CODEC_MAX=2] is the queue (:299), ipi_desc[IPI_MAX] the handler table. ipi_done (the AP send's second half) is set at the entry of the daemon's NEXT VCU_GET_OBJECT (:492), so an AP send returns only after the daemon has come back for another message.

[V] 8. Linux's mtk_vcodec_enc_clock_on(ctx, 0) enables larb7 + VENC0 gate AND larb8 + VENC1 gate (K/mt6885/mtk_vcodec_enc_pm.c:273-279); clock_off disables both (:345-349). The kernel's POWER_ON handler (venc_vcu_if.c:135-148) calls venc_encode_prepare(ctx,0) under the GCE lock, i.e. both cores' clocks for one core-0 job.

[I] 9. In our user-space AP this maps to hw->power(RWVC_BLK_VENC) + hw->power(RWVC_BLK_VENC_C1) with reference counting; whether P03's VENC_C1 block is exactly "VENC1 gate + larb8" (no reset of the second core) is for hw-k02/hw-p03 to confirm - if it is heavier, the AP should only power VENC.

[V] 10. The AP instance cookie (venc_inst / ap_inst_addr) is opaque to the 32-bit daemon, which only stores and echoes it (venc_vcu_if.c:17-25, :360; venc_ipi_msg.h:121-133, :139-160). n2ap_venc uses a 32-bit token so no bits are lost on the daemon side; the kernel itself sends a 64-bit pointer, which only works because it truncates to 32 bits in the compat query struct (:152-157).

[V] 11. Message sizes are bounded by SHARE_BUF_SIZE 80 (uapi/linux/mtk_vcu_controls.h:11); the kernel BUILD_BUG_ONs every encoder message against it (venc_vcu_if.c:79-92). The largest one is ap_ipi_msg_enc at 76.
